conviction_note: The 1 Oct 2026 trading update already gave H1 adjusted EPS (64-68p) and reiterated both EPS guides, and I found nothing unpriced that decides this print. So p_up sits at 53, a slight lean from a strong H1 renewables base and an FY consensus of 183.5p above the guide midpoint, and abs_move_pct is 3.0, the pre-released base. The findings sum to +0.6 against a scaled +0.18. The gap is three small positive inferences, not a contradiction.

new_in_release.expect: H1 adj EPS inside the 64-68p range. Upper half is slightly more likely: last year's 33-37p pre-release printed 36.1p, and H1 renewables output was up ~20%. The market was told this range, so it is worth ~0.

Unknown. FY26/27 168-193p could be narrowed. With a strong H1 and consensus at 183.5p, an upper-half narrowing is slightly more likely than a lower one. The company may also just reiterate, citing the winter still to come.
The interim follows the published dividend plan (FY25/26 interim was 21.4p). Expect ~5-10% growth, already known by formula.
Net debt ~GBP11.5bn was pre-released. Capex >GBP5bn for the year is the plan. No surprise expected.

A possible update on the investment plan beyond GBP33bn (NESO's Beyond 2030 potential +GBP12bn for SSEN Transmission), plus Dogger Bank and Berwick Bank progress. Direction unknown, mildly positive if a plan extension comes without new equity.

findings.finding: SSE pre-released a strong H1 (renewables output ~+20%, H1 adj EPS 64-68p against 36.1p a year ago) but left the wide FY26/27 168-193p range untouched. Consensus is 183.5p, above the 180.5p midpoint. If the range is narrowed at the interims, the upper half is somewhat more likely than the lower.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Reiterations have moved the stock little: 2026-10-01 trading update -0.72%, 2026-05-28 prelims -1.03%, 2026-07-16 Q1 -1.58%. The 2025-11-12 interims moved +16.84%, but that release carried a new 2030 plan and targets, not a narrowing.
findings.why_not_priced: The strong H1 is priced, and consensus at 183.5p already sits in the upper half. What is not priced is whether management narrows the range at H1 rather than at the February Q3 statement. If the market expected an upper-half narrowing, consensus would sit nearer 188-190p. The +3.6% 20-day run-up is modest.
findings.independence: HL consensus 183.5p versus the guide midpoint (https://www.hl.co.uk/shares/share-research/sse-h1-update-strong-start-guidance-reiterated). A Sept 2026 record monthly UK wind output (6.62 TWh) was reported in a search snippet only. Both rest partly on H1 facts that are already public.

findings.finding: A GBP105m non-discretionary buyback by UBS has been running since 12 Oct 2026 and continues through the print, while disclosed shorts are covering (1.5% to 1.3%). Small mechanical support with no crowded short to squeeze.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measurable reaction on prior scrip-offset buybacks. The programme is ~0.3% of market cap over four months.
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced: the programme is public and tiny relative to $77m a day of turnover. It is filed because it is a sourced fact inside the window. It agrees with the covering shorts, so it adds almost nothing beyond the lean.
findings.independence: FCA register shows shorts covering 1.5% to 1.3% (https://www.fca.org.uk/publication/documents/aggregated-current-net-short-positions.csv).

findings.finding: NESO's Beyond 2030 Update (30 Jun 2026) identified a further potential >GBP12bn of SSEN Transmission investment (EGL5, EGL6, Greens-Harburn). The interims are the first full results since then and could fold it into a longer-dated growth outlook.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The interims that introduced the GBP33bn plan and 2029/30 targets (2025-11-12) moved +16.84%. The 30 Jun 2026 Beyond 2030 RNS itself showed no notable move in the baseline history.
findings.why_not_priced: The pipeline was public in June. Whether SSE puts a number or a funding route on it at H1 is unknown, and the company has said nothing about doing so. Its own caveat is that progression needs 'an appropriate regulatory framework', which points to a later update (ED3 plan in December, a CMD). So this stays small. If the market expected a plan extension now, the 60-day run-up would be larger than +11.6% and previews would mention it.
